overview: KE Holdings operates Beike, the leading integrated online-and-offline platform for housing transactions and services in China, built on the infrastructure of its wholly owned legacy brokerage brand Lianjia and an open Agent Cooperation Network (ACN) that connects independent brokerage brands, stores and agents nationwide. The company facilitates existing-home sales, new-home sales, home renovation and furnishing, and home rental services, and reports in RMB under US GAAP. It is dual-primary listed on NYSE (ADS: BEKE) and HKEX (2423.HK, Class A shares, since May 2022), with a VIE/weighted-voting-rights (WVR) structure controlling its China operating entities.

business_model.summary: Beike monetizes an agent/brokerage marketplace: commissions and platform/franchise fees on existing-home sales (largely transactional but with a growing recurring platform-fee tail from connected stores), marketing/sales commissions from real-estate developers for new-home sales (project/cycle-based and historically working-capital intensive), fee-for-service home renovation and furnishing, and property management/leasing fees from home rental (Carefree Rent), which is shifting from gross asset-heavy to net asset-light service-fee recognition. Revenue is largely transaction/volume-driven (tied to China housing GTV) rather than subscription-recurring, though platform/franchise fees and rental management fees provide a steadier base.

revenue_streams.name: Existing-home transaction services
revenue_streams.trend: declining (FY2025 -11.3% YoY; H1 2026 -3.2% YoY, but GTV flat and Q2 2026 revenue +4.5% YoY as volumes recovered)

revenue_streams.name: New-home transaction services
revenue_streams.trend: declining (FY2025 GTV -8.2%; H1 2026 revenue -15.9% YoY, though Q2 2026 GTV returned to +1.2% YoY growth)

revenue_streams.name: Home renovation and furnishing
revenue_streams.trend: declining (H1 2026 revenue -26.4% YoY as company proactively cut low-quality channels; margins improving)

revenue_streams.name: Home rental services (Carefree Rent)
revenue_streams.trend: unit count growing (+34% YoY to >790,000 units) but revenue declining (-8.5% H1 2026) as model shifts to net/asset-light fee recognition

revenue_streams.name: Emerging and other services (financial services, Beihaojia C2M, etc.)

business_model.customer_type: B2C (home buyers, sellers, landlords, tenants, renovation customers) and B2B (real estate developers, independent brokerage brands/stores/agents, renovation/rental service providers)
business_model.geographic_mix: Mainland China only; nationwide coverage across hundreds of cities with concentration in tier-1/tier-2 cities; no material international operations

main_competitors: Local/regional traditional offline brokerage chains and independent agencies
New-home marketing services providers (project-level competitors for developer commissions)
Traffic-focused super-app platforms competing for customer attention/leads
competitive_position.market_position: Largest integrated online-offline housing transaction platform in China by GTV; Lianjia is described as China's leading brokerage brand by service quality; management states ~68% of existing/new-home GTV is generated through connected (non-Lianjia) brokerage brands, evidencing the scale of the open-platform model versus single-brand rivals

moat_factors.description: Agent Cooperation Network incentivizes cross-store/cross-brand collaboration and commission-sharing, making the platform more valuable as more brands, stores and agents join; 279 connected brokerage brands beyond Lianjia
~303 million properties catalogued since 2008, used for listing verification, valuation and AI-assisted search; difficult for new entrants to replicate at scale
Lianjia's 24+ year track record and 'authentic listings' positioning differentiate Beike from traffic-only listing sites plagued by fake listings
SaaS tools (A+ SaaS, Link SaaS), transaction service centers, escrow (eHomePay) and training infrastructure raise switching costs for connected stores/agents once onboarded
eHomePay holds a PBOC-licensed payment/escrow platform, a barrier for unlicensed competitors in payment/escrow services

weaknesses: Revenue is highly correlated with China property transaction volumes (GTV), which have been in multi-year decline/adjustment
New-home segment depends on developer financial health and timely commission payment; counterparty risk from a stressed developer sector
Agent/store count can be volatile (agents -3.1% YoY as of H1 2026) reflecting broader industry contraction
Lower pricing power/thin margins in home renovation business versus established renovation specialists
Mobile MAU has declined YoY (45.7mm in Q2 2026 vs 48.7mm in Q2 2025), raising questions about engagement/customer acquisition cost trends

growth_drivers: Market share gains in existing-home brokerage via productivity improvements per connected store/agent, even as overall industry volumes stagnate (H1 2026 existing-home transaction count +18.6% YoY, outpacing the broader market)
Continued expansion of the connected-brand network (non-Lianjia brands now ~68% of GTV), scaling the asset-light platform-fee model

AI-driven productivity tools (AI home-search assistant, AI CRM, AI-assisted BIM design for renovation, AI-driven Carefree Rent operations) to lower cost-to-serve and improve agent/service-provider efficiency
Asset-light transition in home rental (Carefree Rent net-fee model) reducing capital intensity while unit count under management grows (+34% YoY)
Home renovation and furnishing standardization/centralized procurement to improve margins even as the company deliberately shrinks lower-quality revenue
Shareholder return program: aggressive buybacks (~US$2.99bn repurchased since September 2022, ~14.8% of pre-program shares; ~US$450mm deployed in H1 2026 alone, including first HK-market repurchases)
Beihaojia C2M data/analytics services monetizing Beike's demand-side insights for real estate developers as a newer, less capital-intensive revenue stream

business.description: Total GTV declined 5.0% in FY2025 and transaction volumes remain below prior-cycle peaks; revenue and GTV move together and the new-home market in particular remains in 'ongoing adjustment'

New-home commissions are paid by developers, some of which face liquidity stress in China's broader property-sector downturn; management highlights active monitoring of receivable turnover days (improved to 39 days in Q2 2026 from 51 days a year earlier) as a risk-mitigation KPI
Total agent count fell 3.1% YoY and active agents fell 7.5% YoY as of H1 2026, reflecting industry consolidation that could pressure platform liquidity/listings coverage if it continues
Competes with online listing platforms, traffic-focused apps, offline traditional brokerages and new-home marketing competitors simultaneously across multiple business lines

financial.description: Net revenue swung from -12.0% YoY in H1 2026 to a Q2 2026 return-to-growth in some segments, illustrating sharp quarter-to-quarter swings tied to housing-market sentiment

Adjusted net income materially exceeds GAAP net income in some periods (and the reverse in others, e.g., FY2025 GAAP RMB2.99bn vs non-GAAP RMB5.02bn), so GAAP/non-GAAP divergence needs to be tracked by investors

financial.risk: RMB currency exposure for USD-listed shares/ADS
financial.description: Reports in RMB; USD/HKD investors bear RMB translation risk on both the P&L and converted buyback economics

regulatory.description: KE Holdings is a Cayman Islands holding company; PRC operations are conducted via contractual VIE arrangements and the company is 'controlled through weighted voting rights' (Class B shares, 10 votes each); Chinese regulatory action against VIE structures could materially impair investor control/economic rights

KE was previously named on the SEC's list of issuers facing potential delisting under the HFCAA audit-inspection dispute; the company pursued a Hong Kong dual-primary listing (since May 2022) specifically as a hedge against a US delisting scenario, which materially reduces (but does not eliminate) this risk going forward

Subject to evolving PRC regulations on property transactions, data security/privacy (customer and listings data), and licensing (e.g., eHomePay's PBOC payment license), any of which could raise compliance costs or restrict operations

macro.description: China's broader residential property sector has been in a multi-year contraction/adjustment since 2021-2022; GTV for both existing- and new-home transactions declined again in FY2025 and the new-home market stayed weak into H1 2026
Home-buying decisions are sensitive to household income expectations and job security, both pressured amid China's slower growth environment

Transaction volumes are highly sensitive to PRC central and local government property policy (mortgage rates, down-payment ratios, purchase restrictions, destocking programs); policy can move supportively or restrictively with limited notice

macro_factors.industry_outlook: China's residential real estate transaction market remains in a multi-year adjustment following the 2021-2022 developer liquidity crisis; existing-home transactions have been comparatively more resilient (flat-to-growing in some 2026 quarters) while new-home transactions continue to contract as the primary market works through oversupply; Beike's strategy of gaining share within a shrinking-to-stabilizing pie is the dominant industry narrative
macro_factors.cyclicality: High — revenue is closely linked to housing transaction GTV, which is itself tied to China's property cycle, mortgage policy and broader economic conditions
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High (indirect) — Chinese mortgage rates and down-payment requirements directly affect transaction affordability and volumes, though Beike itself carries low financial leverage
key_input_costs: Cloud/data-center infrastructure (third-party cloud services, e.g., Tencent Cloud)

recent_developments.event: Q2 2026 results: net revenue ~RMB24.5bn (-5.7% YoY) but GAAP net income roughly doubled YoY to ~RMB2.6bn; adjusted net income +74.9% YoY to RMB3.2bn; gross margin rose 6.7pp YoY to 28.6% as cost discipline and improved unit economics took hold; GTV returned to YoY growth (+6.3%); company repurchased ~US$250mm of shares in the quarter, including its first Hong Kong-market repurchases

Interim report shows net revenue down 12.0% YoY to RMB43.4bn but adjusted net income up 49.2% YoY to RMB4.8bn; existing-home transaction count +18.6% YoY (outpacing the market) while new-home GTV fell 17.1% YoY for H1 but returned to growth (+1.2%) in Q2; home renovation revenue cut 26.4% YoY as the company proactively exited lower-quality channels; rental units under Carefree Rent grew 34% YoY to >790,000
Company deployed ~US$450mm under its Share Repurchase Program across NYSE and HKEX; cumulative repurchases since September 2022 reached ~US$2.99bn, about 14.8% of pre-program shares outstanding

Full-year GTV fell 5.0% to RMB3,183.3bn; net revenue grew modestly (+1.2%) to RMB94.6bn despite the GTV decline, aided by home rental and renovation mix shift; GAAP net income fell to RMB2,991mm from RMB4,078mm in 2024 (adjusted net income RMB5,017mm vs RMB7,211mn in 2024); store count grew 18.5% to 61,139 even as agent growth was modest (+4.6%)

Analyst sentiment mixed: Citigroup reiterated Buy (May 2026); Wall Street Zen downgraded to Hold (August 2026) ahead of Q2 earnings; BofA raised its price target to ~$21 following Q4 2025 results; consensus skewed toward Moderate Buy with price targets roughly in the $20-23 range on the NYSE ADS (BEKE) as of mid-2026

items.target: No formal quantitative full-year guidance disclosed
items.notes: Management does not provide specific point or range revenue guidance; commentary is qualitative, emphasizing 'prudent capital allocation and strict operating discipline' and continued focus on unit economics and operational resilience across market conditions

items.target: Continued margin improvement via cost structure optimization
items.notes: Management cites gross margin expansion (+6.7pp YoY in Q2 2026 to 28.6%) and a 14.1% YoY reduction in operating expenses as evidence of a 'healthier operating model'; expects contribution margins across major business lines to keep rising

items.target: Continuation of the Share Repurchase Program (no fixed future dollar target disclosed beyond cumulative figures)
items.notes: ~US$2.99bn repurchased cumulatively through June 2026 (~14.8% of pre-program share count); ~US$450mm repurchased in H1 2026 alone, now including HKEX-market buybacks for the first time

items.target: Continued growth of Carefree Rent asset-light model
items.notes: Units under management grew 34% YoY to over 790,000 as of June 30, 2026, with management emphasizing per-unit economics and risk resilience over gross unit growth

guidance.management_commentary: Management describes H1 2026 as a period of 'gradually establishing a healthier operating model,' citing the Q2 2026 return of GTV to year-over-year growth (+6.3%) and improving contribution margins across all major business lines as evidence of recovery momentum. The outlook section emphasizes prudent capital allocation, operating discipline, and continued investment in AI, organizational mechanisms and service-provider enablement, while explicitly not providing numeric forward guidance; management frames the China housing market adjustment as structural rather than one that the company controls, positioning its strategy around gaining share within a smaller-but-stabilizing pie.

bull_case: Market-share gains in existing-home brokerage are outpacing a declining-to-stabilizing overall market (H1 2026 existing-home transaction count +18.6% YoY), suggesting structural consolidation benefits a scaled platform like Beike

Margin expansion and cost discipline are driving GAAP and adjusted profitability well above revenue growth (Q2 2026 net income roughly doubled YoY despite a revenue decline), indicating operating leverage as the business matures past its land-grab phase

Aggressive and accelerating capital returns (~US$2.99bn cumulative buybacks, ~14.8% of shares, now spanning both NYSE and HKEX) signal management confidence and directly support per-share value even in a flat-to-declining top-line environment

Diversification beyond pure brokerage into home rental (Carefree Rent, asset-light model, +34% unit growth) and renovation provides multiple avenues for monetizing the same customer base and could offset new-home transaction cyclicality over time

Potential optionality from Chinese government property-support policy: any meaningful stimulus to existing-home transaction volumes would disproportionately benefit Beike given its scale and connected-brand network
bear_case: Revenue remains fundamentally tied to China's structurally weaker property transaction volumes, particularly new-home sales, which fell double digits in H1 2026 and show no clear multi-year recovery catalyst

VIE/weighted-voting-rights structure means foreign shareholders do not have direct equity ownership of the PRC operating entities; any adverse PRC regulatory action on VIEs (or control disputes) could materially impair shareholder value regardless of operating performance

Declining agent counts (agents -3.1% YoY, active agents -7.5% YoY) and falling mobile MAU (45.7mm vs 48.7mm YoY) could signal eroding platform engagement/liquidity if the trend persists, undermining the network-effect moat
Developer counterparty risk in new-home transactions remains elevated given the broader stress in China's real estate developer sector, even though receivable turnover days have recently improved

GAAP earnings quality is volatile and materially diverges from non-GAAP adjusted figures across periods (SBC, fair-value changes, impairments), making headline profitability figures harder for investors to rely on consistently
